node_definition.done_when: collapse_section and read_plan with view section both resolve a section whose id sits on a wrapping section element (the shape a-review-dies-where-nobody-is-looking uses), and still resolve one whose id sits on its h2. A section read of that plan lists its sections instead of reporting none. tests/test_section_id_on_its_wrapper_resolves.py builds both shapes in a temporary docs tree, and collapses and reads a section in each. The wrapper cases fail at the base. Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
